contentGeneration.title: Content Generation
contentGeneration.short: You are starting from scratch and want strong, fresh ideas for new products and services.
contentGeneration.long: Need fresh ideas fast? Our content and idea service uses AI to help creators, founders, and teams find new ideas in seconds. From product names and social posts to startup concepts and campaign slogans, you get strong ideas built around your goals and your audience. No more creative blocks, just more options than you can use.

detail.intro: Most teams do not have an idea problem. They have a throughput problem. The concepts that would have worked never get written down, because the hours it takes to produce fifty viable options are hours nobody has. Our content generation service closes that gap: we build the prompt systems, brand constraints, and review loops that let your team produce a large volume of on-brand starting points and then choose well among them.
detail.body: This is not a request to hand your voice over to a model. We start from what you already sound like, encode it, and use AI to widen the field of options rather than to replace the judgment that picks the winner. The output is a working system your team keeps, not a one-time delivery of copy.

steps.title: Capture your voice
steps.body: We study your copy, positioning, and audience research and write down your brand voice and tone. That written spec is the bar every new option has to clear, so making more never costs you a consistent voice.

steps.title: Build the generation system
steps.body: We assemble prompt chains, reference libraries, and evaluation criteria tuned to your categories, whether that is product naming, campaign lines, long-form editorial, or social. You get the system, the prompts, and the reasoning behind both.

steps.title: Generate, filter, and hand over
steps.body: We run the system against your live briefs, filter the output down to the strongest candidates, and train your team to operate it without us. Knowledge transfer is part of the engagement, not an upsell.

deliverables: A written guide to your brand voice
Prompt libraries tuned to your work
A filtered set of ready-to-use concepts from your live briefs
A working session so your team can run the system independently

faq.q: Will it sound like generic AI copy?
faq.a: That is the failure mode we build against. The voice specification and reference library are what keep generated options inside your brand rather than inside the model's defaults. Generic output usually means nobody encoded the constraints, and encoding them is the first phase of the work.

faq.q: Do we keep what you build?
faq.a: Yes. Everything we build is documented and handed over. The point of the engagement is that your team can keep generating after it ends.

faq.q: Which models do you use?
faq.a: We select per task rather than committing to one vendor, and we tell you why. Reasoning-heavy work and high-volume drafting have different cost and quality profiles.

faq.q: How do you check the facts?
faq.a: Generated drafts are treated as candidates, never as finished claims. Any factual assertion goes through human review before it ships, and we build that checkpoint into the workflow rather than leaving it to discipline.

contentGeneration.metaDescription: AI content generation from ArsonistAI. We build the prompt systems, brand constraints, and review loops your team keeps and operates independently.

conceptVisualization.title: Concept Visualization
conceptVisualization.short: You have rough ideas and need detail and strong visuals to go with them.
conceptVisualization.long: Bring your ideas to life with our concept visualization service. We use the newest AI tools to turn rough concepts into bold, high-impact visuals, fast. Whether you need product designs, moodboards, 3D interfaces, or campaign images, we help you get from a loose idea to a clear picture of it in minutes.

detail.intro: The distance between an idea described in a meeting and an idea everyone can see is where most projects stall. Written concepts get nodded at and then interpreted six different ways. Our concept visualization service compresses that distance: we turn abstract direction into concrete, high-fidelity visuals fast enough to use inside the decision, not after it.
detail.body: We work on product design, moodboards, 3D interfaces, scenes, and campaign art. The aim is shared understanding. When people can point at an image, the question stops being what did you mean and becomes whether this is right.

steps.title: Pin down the direction
steps.body: We work from your brief, references, and constraints to establish what the visual has to communicate and to whom. Vague inputs produce vague images, so this step is where we get specific about the decision the visual needs to support.

steps.title: Generate at breadth
steps.body: We produce multiple distinct visual directions rather than refining a single guess. Seeing three real options side by side surfaces preferences that no amount of discussion will.

steps.title: Refine to fidelity
steps.body: Once a direction is chosen, we push it to the fidelity you actually need, whether that is a pitch-ready render, a moodboard for a design team, or a set of assets for a campaign.

deliverables: Several distinct visual directions
Renders or moodboards in full detail
The source files and prompts
A documented rationale for why each direction reads the way it does

faq.q: How fast is the first round?
faq.a: First directions typically land within days rather than weeks, because generating breadth is cheap once the brief is specific. The timeline depends far more on how quickly the brief gets pinned down than on production.

faq.q: Can you match our visual identity?
faq.a: Yes. Working inside an established identity is the common case. We build a reference set from your existing assets and treat it as a constraint on every direction we generate.

faq.q: Do we get the source files?
faq.a: Yes, along with the prompts and reference images behind them, so your team can continue the direction without starting over.

faq.q: Does this replace a design team?
faq.a: No. It is a way to get a design team to the right starting point faster. The judgment about which direction is right remains a human decision, and usually yours.

conceptVisualization.metaDescription: Turn abstract direction into high-fidelity visuals fast. Product design, moodboards, 3D interfaces, and campaign imagery from ArsonistAI.

explorationScaling.title: Exploration Scaling
explorationScaling.short: You have some ideas on screen and want a wider set of variations.
explorationScaling.long: Widen your creative range with our exploration scaling service. If you have a solid concept or a few visual ideas, we use the newest AI models to quickly make strong variations in style, structure, or concept, and grow your first direction into a much broader set of options.

detail.intro: A single good concept is a risk. Without alternatives, you cannot tell whether it is the right answer or the first answer. Our exploration scaling service takes a direction you already believe in and expands it into a broad, structured landscape of variations, so the option you ship is one you chose rather than one you settled for.
detail.body: Variation can be stylistic, structural, or conceptual. We decide with you which axis actually matters for the decision in front of you, then generate along it deliberately instead of producing noise.

steps.title: Define the axis of variation
steps.body: Scaling in every direction at once produces a pile, not a decision. We identify which dimension is genuinely open, whether that is visual style, information structure, or the underlying concept.

steps.title: Generate systematically
steps.body: We produce variations along the chosen axis at volume, keeping every other variable fixed so comparisons are meaningful. This is what separates a real exploration from a random sample.

steps.title: Cluster and narrow
steps.body: We group the output into coherent families, name what distinguishes them, and narrow to a shortlist your team can actually evaluate in a room.

deliverables: A structured set of options, laid out along one named axis of variation
Families of options, each explained
A shortlist sized for one meeting
The generation setup, so you can rerun the exploration later

faq.q: How many variations do we get?
faq.a: Enough to make the axis legible, which is usually dozens rather than a handful. What you receive is the clustered shortlist, not the raw pile.

faq.q: What do you need from us to start?
faq.a: One direction you already believe in, and a clear statement of what decision the exploration is meant to inform.

faq.q: Does this work for non-visual work?
faq.a: Yes. The same method works for site structure, messaging, and product concepts as well. The axis of variation changes, but the way we work does not.

faq.q: What if none of them are right?
faq.a: That is a useful outcome, and it usually means the axis was wrong rather than the execution. We reset the axis and rerun, which is fast once the system is built.

explorationScaling.metaDescription: Expand one direction into a structured landscape of variations, clustered and narrowed to a shortlist your team can actually evaluate.

experienceOptimization.title: Experience Optimization
experienceOptimization.short: Audit your digital products and make them easier to use.
experienceOptimization.long: Improve every point where users touch your digital product. We audit with AI and proven UX principles to find friction, missed chances, and places to engage users more deeply. From clear screens to smooth flows, we find what works and what does not, then suggest smart fixes you can act on.

detail.intro: Products rarely fail at one dramatic moment. They lose people across dozens of small frictions that no one inside the team can still see. Our experience optimization service audits your digital product against AI analysis and established UX principles, then returns a prioritized, specific list of what to change and why.
detail.body: The deliverable is not a document that describes your product back to you. It is a ranked set of changes, each tied to the friction it removes and the evidence behind the claim.

steps.title: Audit the current experience
steps.body: We walk the real flows the way a user does, instrumented with AI analysis and heuristic evaluation, and record where attention breaks, where intent gets lost, and where the interface asks for more than it needs.

steps.title: Rank by impact and cost
steps.body: Every finding is scored against how much friction it removes and how expensive it is to fix. A long undifferentiated list of problems is not actionable, so we do not deliver one.

steps.title: Specify the fixes
steps.body: For the top findings we produce concrete recommendations, and where it helps, the revised interface itself, so your team is implementing a decision rather than interpreting a critique.

deliverables: A list of findings, each scored by its impact and by what it would cost to fix
Evidence behind every finding
Clear fixes for the top problems
Redesigns where words fall short

faq.q: Do you need our analytics?
faq.a: It helps and it sharpens the ranking, but it is not required. A heuristic and AI-assisted audit finds most structural friction without it.

faq.q: How long does an audit take?
faq.a: It scales with the number of distinct flows rather than screens. Scoping starts with a conversation about which journeys actually matter to the business.

faq.q: Will you implement the changes?
faq.a: We can, and product design is a separate service if you want the fixes built rather than specified. The audit stands on its own either way.

faq.q: What if we disagree with a finding?
faq.a: Every finding ships with its evidence so you can argue with it. A finding you can not interrogate is not worth acting on.

experienceOptimization.metaDescription: A UX audit that returns ranked, evidence-backed fixes scored by impact and cost, not a document describing your product back to you.

productDesign.title: Product Design
productDesign.short: Our team will guide you through every stage of building your product.
productDesign.long: Transform your ideas into beautifully functional products with our AI-powered product design service. We combine the speed of AI with the insight of human-centered design to help you visualize, iterate, and refine digital experiences faster than ever.

detail.intro: Our product design service pairs the speed of AI with the judgment of human-centered design. You get the pace that makes exploring real options affordable, and the structural thinking that keeps a fast-moving product coherent instead of piling up decisions that nobody meant to make.
detail.body: We cover the full arc: early concept, site structure, interface design, and design systems. Which parts you need depends on where the product is today, and we scope the work to that instead of to a fixed package.

steps.title: Frame the problem
steps.body: We establish what the product is for, who it serves, and what success looks like in measurable terms before anything gets drawn. Most design problems that resist solving are framing problems wearing a costume.

steps.title: Design and iterate
steps.body: We move through concept, structure, and interface, using AI to make each iteration cheap enough that we test real alternatives instead of defending the first one.

steps.title: Systematize and hand off
steps.body: We turn the result into components, patterns, and written decisions, so the product stays coherent after we leave and your engineers are not guessing at intent from a mockup.

deliverables: A written problem frame and goals
Designs for the flows that matter
Documented parts for engineers
The reasoning, written down

faq.q: Can you use our design system?
faq.a: Yes, and it is usually the better path. We extend what you have rather than replacing it, unless replacing it is genuinely the cheaper option.

faq.q: What do engineers get?
faq.a: Designs, components, and the reasons behind the main decisions. Writing those reasons down is what keeps the intent from getting lost while it is built.

faq.q: How is AI actually used here?
faq.a: Mainly to make iteration cheap. It generates options, tests structures, and makes variations fast enough that exploring is affordable. The structural decisions stay with people.

faq.q: Can you work with our designers?
faq.a: Yes. Embedding with an existing team is common, and the systematization step is designed to leave that team better equipped than it started.

productDesign.metaDescription: Product design pairing AI iteration speed with human-centered judgment. Concept, information architecture, interface, and design system work.

operationsConsulting.title: Operations Consulting
operationsConsulting.short: Use AI to make your business run better and grow with less effort.
operationsConsulting.long: Run leaner and grow with our AI operations consulting service. We use the newest AI tools to study how work flows, find the waste, and give you advice, backed by data, that helps your team get more done and spend less.

detail.intro: Most of the waste in how a company runs is invisible from inside, because the workarounds have been normal for years. Our AI operations service maps how work really moves through your team, finds where time and money leak, and gives you advice specific enough to act on this quarter.
detail.body: We are interested in the processes your team actually runs, not the ones on the org chart. That distinction is usually where the recoverable cost is hiding.

steps.title: Map the real workflow
steps.body: We document how work actually moves, including the spreadsheets, side channels, and manual steps that no process diagram admits to. This is where most of the recoverable time turns out to live.

steps.title: Find the leaks
steps.body: We use AI analysis to identify repetitive work, handoff delays, and decisions that stall for reasons nobody owns, then quantify what each one costs.

steps.title: Recommend and sequence
steps.body: You get recommendations ranked by return and difficulty, sequenced into an order that actually works, because some fixes are prerequisites for others.

deliverables: A map of how work moves today
Every inefficiency we find, with what each one costs you written down
Ranked fixes with return and effort
An order to do the work in

faq.q: Is this about replacing staff with AI?
faq.a: No. It is about finding the repetitive work that is consuming people who should be doing something harder. Where automation is the right answer we will say so, and where it is not we will say that too.

faq.q: How much access do you need?
faq.a: Enough to observe real workflows, which usually means interviews and access to the tools work passes through. We scope access explicitly at the start.

faq.q: What size organization is this for?
faq.a: The method scales from a single team to a department. Below a certain size the recoverable cost usually does not justify the engagement, and we will tell you if that is the case.

faq.q: Do you help with the fixes?
faq.a: Yes, as a separate engagement. The assessment is deliberately useful on its own so you are not locked into a follow-on.

operationsConsulting.metaDescription: We map how work actually moves through your organization, quantify where time and money leak, and sequence the fixes worth making first.

openclawInstallation.title: Openclaw Installation & Integration
openclawInstallation.short: Full Openclaw install and integration, with 30 days of support.
openclawInstallation.long: We handle the full Openclaw install and integration for your environment, with 30 days of support so you are covered from day one. It includes setup, configuration, and knowledge transfer, all for $3,000.

detail.intro: We handle the full Openclaw install and integration, built around your environment, and support it for 30 days so you are covered from the day it goes live. Setup, configuration, and knowledge transfer are all included, for a price of $3,000.
detail.body: The point is not just a working install. It is that your team understands the configuration well enough to change it without calling us, which is what the knowledge transfer step exists to guarantee.

steps.title: Assess the environment
steps.body: We review your current stack, access model, and limits so the install fits what you really run, not a reference design that assumes something else.

steps.title: Install and configure
steps.body: We handle the full installation and tune the configuration to your environment, including the integration points with the tools your team already uses.

steps.title: Transfer and support
steps.body: We document the configuration and walk your team through it, then stay available for 30 days to handle whatever surfaces once real usage starts.

deliverables: Openclaw, installed and configured
Links to the tools you already use
Written docs for the setup, plus a live session that walks your team through it
30 days of support after launch

faq.q: What does the engagement cost?
faq.a: It costs $3,000, which covers the install, the integration, the setup, knowledge transfer, and 30 days of support after it goes live.

faq.q: What does support cover?
faq.a: Issues arising from the installation and configuration we delivered, including the problems that only appear once the team is using it for real.

faq.q: How long does installation take?
faq.a: It depends on the complexity of your environment and how quickly access is granted. The environment assessment gives you a firm timeline before work starts.

faq.q: What happens after the 30 days?
faq.a: Your team owns a documented setup they understand. We can arrange ongoing support if you want it, but the handover is built so you should not need it.

openclawInstallation.metaDescription: Full Openclaw installation and integration tailored to your environment, including configuration, knowledge transfer, and 30 days of support.

claudeCursorTraining.title: Claude Code and Cursor Training
claudeCursorTraining.short: Get your whole team up to speed on building with Claude Code and Cursor.
claudeCursorTraining.long: Hands-on training on using Claude Code and Cursor well. We cover the best habits, prompts, and setup so your team can ship faster with help from AI. We shape each session around your stack and the way your team works.

detail.intro: Structured training on using Claude Code and Cursor well in real day-to-day work. We cover the habits, prompts, and setup choices that split teams who ship faster with AI from teams who just write more code and then review more of it.
detail.body: Sessions are tailored to your stack and your processes. Generic AI training produces generic results, so we build the material around the codebase your team actually works in.

steps.title: Assess how your team works
steps.body: We review your stack, review process, and current AI usage to find where the tools will pay off and where they are already creating rework.

steps.title: Run tailored sessions
steps.body: Training uses your own code and the way you work, not toy examples. Every exercise comes from work your team will recognize.

steps.title: Establish working practice
steps.body: We leave written conventions for when to reach for AI help, how to review what it writes, and where it should stay out of the way.

deliverables: Training built on your own codebase
Written rules for prompting and review that your team can follow
Guidance on how the tools fit into the way you build software now
A written guide your team keeps

faq.q: How technical must the team be?
faq.a: The training targets working developers. We adjust depth to experience level, but it assumes people who write and review code.

faq.q: Claude Code, Cursor, or both?
faq.a: Whichever fits your workflow. They solve similar problems in different ways, and part of the training is knowing which one to use and when.

faq.q: How long is the training?
faq.a: It scales with team size and how deep you want to go. Scoping starts with a conversation about your current workflow and where it hurts.

faq.q: Can it be delivered remotely?
faq.a: Yes. Remote delivery is the default, and sessions are structured to work that way rather than being an in-person format moved online.

claudeCursorTraining.metaDescription: Structured Claude Code and Cursor training built around your codebase and review process, so your team ships faster instead of reviewing more.

chatbotAudit.title: Chatbot Audit
chatbotAudit.short: Test your customer support chatbot before it talks to a single customer in your name.
chatbotAudit.long: Before your support chatbot goes live, we ask it the questions that catch bots out and check every answer against your own policies and product pages. Every price, date, phone number, and link it gives is compared with your documents, and anything it made up is flagged. You get a plain-English report you can read in ten minutes. From $295.

detail.intro: Your support chatbot is about to talk to customers in your name. The questions that matter most are the ones your documents do not answer. A bot that invents a refund policy, a price, or a warranty does more harm than one that says it does not know, and customers will hold you to what it said. Most of the audit is aimed at that failure.
detail.body: The checks are rules wherever a rule can decide. Where only judgment can tell whether an answer is wrong, an AI model looks for contradictions with your documents, quotes the exact line it relied on, and is labeled as a model's verdict so you can check it yourself. Anything the checks cannot settle is listed for a person to read and is never counted as a pass.

steps.title: Write the questions
steps.body: We build about 60 questions from your documents: ones they answer, ones close to them that they do not, policies you do not have, requests outside the bot's job, attempts to make it break its rules, and questions about one customer's own order. You approve the list before anything is sent to your bot.

steps.title: Check every answer
steps.body: Questions go to your bot one at a time, some as short conversations, because a bot that is fine with one message can be talked round over three. Every price, percentage, number of days, date, phone number, email address, and link in its replies is compared with your documents. If it is not there, we flag it.

steps.title: Rank what to fix
steps.body: You get one report that opens in any browser and prints cleanly: the pass and fail counts, the three most serious failures in plain words, then every question with the bot's exact reply and the reason for its verdict. A short call or written note covers what to fix first.

deliverables: A report of every question with the bot's exact reply
The three most serious failures, explained in plain words at the top of the report
The question set, so you can run the same test again after every change you make
A short call or written note on what to fix first, and in what order to fix it

faq.q: What does it cost?
faq.a: $295 for a 30-question check in 3 days, $650 for the full 60-question audit in 5 days, and $950 for the full audit plus a retest after your fixes, delivered within 14 days including the time you take to make them. Fixing the bot is separate work, quoted once you have seen the report.

faq.q: What do you need?
faq.a: The documents the bot is meant to answer from, such as policies, shipping and returns, product facts, and contact details. A way to reach the bot, either the address it answers on or the web page its chat window is on. And written confirmation that you own the bot or are allowed to have it tested.

faq.q: Is it a security test?
faq.a: No. It includes a basic set of attempts to make the bot break its rules, but it is not a security or penetration test, and it is not a load test. Questions are sent one at a time with a pause between them.

faq.q: Is a pass a guarantee?
faq.a: No. A pass is one good answer, not a promise. Each question is asked once, and a bot can answer differently next time. The question set is yours to keep, so you can run it again after every change.

chatbotAudit.metaDescription: Test your customer support chatbot before launch. Every answer is checked against your own documents, and invented prices, policies, and links are flagged.
